newsitem.title: USA: ALPINE SKIING-WIBERG THE BIG WORLD CUP WINNER AT MAMMOTH LAKES.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-WIBERG THE BIG WORLD CUP WINNER AT MAMMOTH LAKES.

text.p: Pernilla Wiberg earned a triple victory on a double day of World Cup racing at Mammoth Mountain Friday, triumphing beyond her own ambition and comprehension.
The dynamic little Swede placed third in the morning super g, clinching the season's overall title, then won the afternoon slalom to claim the season's slalom crown.

"It's amazing," Wiberg said. "My goal this season was to win the slalom cup. It was an extra surprise to also win the overall cup. I don't understand it yet, I think I need to sleep on it. Maybe in Vail when I actually get the cups, I will understand.
Katja Seizinger of Germany won the super g race but was blocked from repeating as overall champion by Wiberg's third-place finish.
"I'm not disappointed," Seizinger said. "I've had a great season and I'm still in second place in the overall."

Gusty winds Thursday forced postponement of the super-g to Friday morning, followed by an already scheduled slalom in the afternoon. Racing conditions on both courses were ideal with fast, firm snow, calm winds and fair skies.

In the slalom, Wiberg posted the second fastest time in the 51-gate first leg, 38.07 seconds, then had the only time below 40 seconds on the 53-gate second leg for a combined winning time of 1 minute, 17.90 seconds.
"My second slalom run today was one of my best runs of the season," said Wiberg. "I wanted to give it my best shot. I felt I was a little bit out but that means I was going very fast."
Sabine Egger of Austria, the leader after the first run, finished the second leg in 40.43 for a second-place finish in a combined time of 1:18.15.
Italy's Lara Magoni was third -- three places ahead of teammate Deborah Compagnoni, the race favourite who had won the slalom and giant slalom at last February's world championships.

The racers began the day flying through a 35-gate super g course from Mammoth's Cornice Bowl into Fascination run. Seizinger's winning time of 1 minute, 16.08 seconds was built on fastest times at all calculated intermediate points, the first by nearly a second. That first interval time reflected her aggressive line in the steep first section of the course.
"I took a risky line and it worked," said Seizinger. "The course was demanding, especially at the top. It had a nice finish."
Hilde Gerg of Germany was second in 1:17.67. "It was the first time I've skied slalom and super-g in one day," she said after finishing in 15th place in the slalom.

Wiberg's super-g time of 1:17.72 earned her third place and an uncatchable lead in the overall standings. After the super g she had 1,615 points overall and at the end of the day she had 1,715 points.
Seizinger, in second overall, had 1,104 points at the end of the day. Even if Seizinger won all the races at the World Cup finals in Vail, Colorado, next week, she could not match Wiberg's points.

Wiberg, who has 670 points in the slalom standings, clinched the season title when second-placed Claudia Riegler of New Zealand crashed at the top of her first run. She has 389 slalom points. Compagnoni, in third place with 367 points, was already out of contention for the season slalom title.
